reasons: The cited text in § 7.2 imposes a reverse MFN squarely on Customer (obligation to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer for Vendor's benefit), which is exactly the direction the rule flags, and no Vendor-granted MFN is being disturbed.
The obligation is open-ended — no product scope, no term limit, no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it sits at the walk-away position, making the deviation status correct.
The redline deletes only p0026, which contains nothing but the offending obligation, so the edit is minimal and directionally correct per the redline guidance ('delete the obligation on Customer').

The comment matches the required tone: first person plural, concise, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the narrow fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) without lecturing.
Deterministic check confirms the operation applies; the only unverifiable element is the cross-reference to § 12.3, which is supportive context rather than the basis of the finding.
